nus v0.0.1-preview.10

A terminal, browser and workspace in one application.

Channel: **preview** · Source: `02739de4c6c8357b07ab43a8a48a47b3094ff83d`

## Changes

- **Assistants in the sidebar (the Ledger).** A tab running Claude, Codex or another assistant shows what it is doing under its title: working with its elapsed time and current tool, waiting with the question it is asking, or done with the files it changed. Claude's permission prompts can be answered from the sidebar (Allow, Deny, Always); the answer is the keystroke the assistant's own prompt takes, so the terminal and the sidebar stay in step. The top strip counts waiting and working assistants.
- **`nus hook`.** Assistants report through their own hook systems: `nus hook install claude|codex` adds nus's hooks beside the user's (a backup is kept; `uninstall` removes only nus's). Settings · Assistants · Connections offers the command for review. Programs that send desktop notifications (OSC 9, OSC 777) are shown as waiting with their words.
- **One profile per channel.** Rebuilt, redownloaded and moved copies share `installs/<channel>/shared` instead of starting over. The most recently used profile moves in on first launch when no nus holds it. A copy can keep its own profile (Settings · Updates · Profile). Welcome shows once per version.
- **Home.** Clicking a row opens that row (rows naming other tabs were missing while the frame drew, so clicks landed one row early). The `nus` wordmark is a latched button: press for home, press again or go back to return. The home line and the palette follow CURSOR's shape, color, blink and weight.
- **Stopping processes.** The ports board's stop button opens the row so its confirmation is visible; before, a stop that needed confirming did nothing.
- **Back and forward.** The swipe overlay has styles (arrow, arrow and words, edge band, none) and distances, shows where a swipe goes or that it goes nowhere, and one swipe no longer fires twice.
- **Panes and windows.** Layout changes go through one director with undo and redo; pane mode (Ctrl+Alt+P) and drop zones move and swap panes; tabs move between windows with their shells and pages intact.
- **Shell colors** from the theme's signal family, in OKLCH, by random choice or by folder.
- **Finish Work.** The coffee in the header keeps the machine awake until work you started finishes, then gives power management back.
- **Interstitials.** Error, warning and interruption pages read as a shell transcript, with the safe command as the default.
- **Intelligence.** One level, Instant to Max, for assistant launches, shown as an atom in Settings · Assistants.

[Candidate review notes, compatibility and known limitations](https://github.com/cbassuarez/nus/blob/02739de4c6c8357b07ab43a8a48a47b3094ff83d/docs/releases/v0.0.1-preview.10.md)

nus v0.0.1-preview.9

A terminal, browser and workspace in one application.

Channel: **preview** · Source: `baebf88bf419031ecb5567d436c8a6040f6182fd`

## Changes

- Optional tools install into separate profile directories, verify their expected files, report start/success/failure, and wake the UI when finished. Removing a tool preserves other tools and externally managed installations.
- Corrected Taplo asset URLs, native gzip/zip extraction, executable permissions, and profile-local npm/Go installation. Missing package managers receive actionable errors. Newly installed language servers become available to existing buffers and prompts.
- Notices outside the editor appear as toasts instead of disappearing into an absent editor status row.
- Failed main-frame navigation keeps the requested destination visible, including redirects; failed subframes do not replace the page address.
- Local pages keep Plot’s dashed boundary without the additional colored loading strip. Loading state follows Chromium’s lifecycle and settles after completion or failure.
- Sidebar hover runs before page-specific pointer handling, clears stale hide timers, and resamples the pointer when focus returns on supported desktops.
- App Icon settings includes selectable artwork cards for the standard faces and earned Mercury. The selection persists; choosing another icon does not remove the Mercury badge.

[Candidate review notes, compatibility and known limitations](https://github.com/cbassuarez/nus/blob/baebf88bf419031ecb5567d436c8a6040f6182fd/docs/releases/v0.0.1-preview.9.md)

nus v0.0.1-preview.8

A terminal, browser and workspace in one application.

Channel: **preview** · Source: `4f351127083717b40370231027058aab540f70b3`

## Changes

- Plot replaces local-site warning tape with four corner markers and quiet survey lines, including matching address and status marks.
- Radiance adds a continuous loading bar with a real HDR highlight on supported native surfaces; stalled loads hold their position and completed loads settle without idle redraws.
- First-window profile onboarding opens automatically again, without repeating in secondary or completed-profile windows.
- Unified reading lists, saved commands, Markdown/JSON/CSV/text viewers, import flow, and Station Port Control improvements.
- Video PiP follows the stream aspect ratio and offers configurable leave/return behavior.
- GitHub update discovery, explicit installation, retained-package recovery, versioned profiles and component compatibility checks.
- Local Mercury claims, encrypted nus-owned sensitive state, local secret redaction, and cross-platform process/file handling fixes.

[Candidate review notes, compatibility and known limitations](https://github.com/cbassuarez/nus/blob/4f351127083717b40370231027058aab540f70b3/docs/releases/v0.0.1-preview.8.md)

## Changes

- A first-open Atlas arrival with perspective star acceleration and clearer Welcome for new and returning installs.
- Themed pin tiles and a palette-only Start/New Tab option.
- Saved reading copies, resume positions and configured encrypted library sync.
- Procedural sky and stars with approximate Sun and Moon motion.
- Stricter release metadata checks and packaging validation.
